temperature_range: 200 ºC for ALD, 430 °C for thermal reduction
summary: Nickel oxide thin films were synthesized by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using NiCp2 and O3 precursors. After a thermal reduction process at 430 °C in a hydrogen atmosphere, the NiO films were converted to metallic Ni. The thickness of the films varied from 250 to 2000 cycles, resulting in different morphologies such as Ni islands and antidot arrays due to dewetting. The study investigated the magnetic properties and dewetting dynamics of the Ni films.
evidence: Abstract. Nickel oxide thin films with different thicknesses were synthesized by atomic layer deposition . After a thermal reduction process, under a controlled atmosphere of hydrogen, it was possible to convert nickel oxide to metallic nickel . The different thicknesses were obtained for 250 to 2000 cycles of NiCp 2/O3. The Ni thin films were characterized by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and by Magneto -Optical Kerr effect measurements. Micromagnetic simulations have been performed to investigate the mechanism of reversion of these films.
